column3: The Hebrew asks about the days of his life’s years; BSB names only years.
The Hebrew shifts to first person for what he eats and drinks; BSB continues “he”.
The Hebrew says to cross the Jordan a little way with the king; BSB specifies a distance “past the Jordan”.
The Hebrew leaves the returning man unnamed and calls his destination “his place”; BSB supplies Barzillai and says “home”.
The Hebrew calls the taking a stealing; BSB says “take you away secretly”.
The Hebrew uses singular “me” and “you” for the groups when speaking of kinship and anger; BSB uses plural “our” and “you”.
The Hebrew shifts the groups into singular “I”, “you”, and “my king”; BSB uses plural pronouns. It compares their “word” as harder, where BSB describes pressing harder.
